page: Amazon Web Services z1d.12xlarge is a memory-optimized Nitro-based virtual server designed for compute-intensive workloads that require sustained high clock speeds alongside substantial memory. The instance is powered by dedicated Intel Xeon 8151 processors on the x86_64 architecture, providing 24 physical cores and 48 vCPUs with hyper-threading enabled. These processors feature a sustained all-core clock speed of 4.0 GHz, supported by 32 KB L1 data cache, 1.0 MB L2 cache, and a 24 MB L3 cache. Standard instruction set extensions including AVX, AVX-512F, AES, BMI2, and ADX are supported.

The system is equipped with 384.0 GB of DDR4 memory running at 3 GHz, delivering an 8:1 memory-to-core ratio of 8.0 GB per vCPU. Local storage is provided via 1,800 GB of NVMe SSD instance storage. Networking features a baseline bandwidth of 25 Gbps. The instance contains zero GPUs and includes zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Benchmark evaluations indicate strong memory subsystem throughput. In uncached large block tests (256 MB), read bandwidth achieved 215.38 GB/sec and write bandwidth reached 92.12 GB/sec, placing memory throughput in the top 25% tier alongside a PassMark memory score of 2,812.58. General processing metrics, including a PassMark CPU score of 44,393.51, a Geekbench multi-core score of 11,997.0, and a stress-ng multi-core metric of 52,390.69, perform within the middle 50% tier. LLM text generation throughput falls within the bottom 25% tier due to the absence of dedicated GPU hardware acceleration.

Cost efficiency is supported by high per-core performance paired with large RAM and integrated NVMe capacity, which reduces the need for supplemental external storage attachments in high-throughput environments. The instance is suited for relational database workloads, in-memory caches, electronic design automation (EDA), financial modeling, and build pipelines requiring high CPU clock speeds and low-latency storage.
